source.title: Hold your horses: a dynamic computational role for the subthalamic nucleus in decision making.

confidence_rationale: Canonical computational model showing cortical conflict drives a DYNAMIC, adaptive threshold via the cortico-subthalamic-pallidal loop -- grounds ARC-063's adaptive-threshold (not fixed) requirement. Confidence mid: it is a response-selection model, not rule-availability, and is a simulation rather than direct measurement.
failure_signatures: The threshold modulated is on response EXECUTION timing, not on rule availability; the model has no representation of abstract rules competing for admission.

The model predicts that without the STN dynamic-threshold pathway, multiple competing options produce premature responding -- so a REE tolerance-gate lacking an adaptive (conflict-sensitive) component, not just a fixed bar, would fail under rule competition.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Incorporating the STN into a basal-ganglia network model, increased cortical response conflict produces dynamic adjustments in the response threshold via cortico-subthalamic-pallidal pathways ('hold your horses'), reducing premature responding when multiple responses compete.
mapping.ree_translation: ARC-063's tolerance gate must be ADAPTIVE, not a fixed bar: when several candidate rules compete (or exceptions accumulate), the availability threshold should rise so the agent samples longer before committing a rule to the active set. Frank's cortico-subthalamic dynamic-threshold loop is the computational template for that adaptivity.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The model gates response execution under motor-response conflict; it contains no abstract-rule layer. REE transfers the adaptive-threshold computation to rule availability -- a domain the model never simulated.
mapping.source_context: Neural-network simulation of basal-ganglia / STN dynamics, validated against Parkinson's response-selection deficits and dopaminergic pharmacological challenge.

confidence_components.notes: Foundational, repeatedly empirically-confirmed model. Mapping/transfer discounted for the response-vs-rule target gap and simulation (vs measurement) status.
